reason: I'd try a free one on the commute since the chips mean I don't have to write an essay about my mood. But I paid for Calm and quit in a month, and nothing here tells me I'd stick with this one any better.
objection: If I have to explain how I feel every time before it plays anything, I'll stop opening it on the bad days, which are the days it's for.
would_change_my_mind: A one-tap 'play what worked last time' for the commute, so it's ready without me typing.

v1.why: The menu, coins and someone else's example chat feel like admin before I can just listen.

v2.why: Cleaner and it's my own session, but I'd still drift off after a few weeks like with Calm.

v3.why: Words-based progress is nicer, but it asks me to check in even more, which is the part I avoid.

reason: The wearable option got my attention so I'd poke at it. I'm not paying a company to hold notes about my mental state when nothing on the screens says where they go or who reads them.
objection: What happens to what I tell it about how I feel, and does it end up training something or getting sold?
would_change_my_mind: A plain privacy page saying my words and check-ins stay mine, can be deleted, and aren't used for training, plus a real Oura connection showing my HRV next to the sessions.

v1.why: Percentages with arrows look like made-up numbers, not my ring's data.

v2.why: Better start, but still no real data from my watch so the 'progress' means nothing to me.

v3.why: Wearable off-by-default and a private journal are the right instincts, but readings are examples until it actually connects.

reason: Free sessions at bedtime, sure, I'll see if my sleep score moves. I've never paid for one of these and YouTube rain sounds already work most nights.
objection: Is this actually better than a free sleep video, or just a fancier way to get the same thing?
would_change_my_mind: Seeing my own sleep score go up for two weeks on nights I used it versus nights I didn't.

v1.why: The coin counter everywhere makes me feel like I'm about to be charged.

v2.why: The free tier with tabs is easy enough to keep for the odd bad night.

v3.why: Same as v2 and the wearable question suggests it might one day read my sleep score.

reason: An AI writing scripts about my anxiety is exactly what I don't want, and I've got free stuff from actual people on YouTube. Money's tight and this is the first thing I'd cut.
objection: I already have free apps and YouTube, and those were made by a person who knows what they're doing.
would_change_my_mind: If a therapist or clinician I'd heard of had written or reviewed what it says, and a friend I trust said it helped.

v1.why: 'Generative Wellness Care' and a coin balance is everything I distrust in one screen.

v2.why: Less cluttered, still an AI making mental health content.

v3.why: The 'Why?' on changes is the most honest bit, but it doesn't change that it's AI-made.

reason: At bedtime I want to tap a sleep story and close my eyes, not chat with an AI about how I feel. A synthetic voice whispering a script written for me a minute ago sounds a bit creepy.
objection: AI meditation voices sound flat and generic, and I don't want one in my ear as I fall asleep.
would_change_my_mind: Hearing a sample voice and soundscape that's genuinely as good as my current sleep app, playable in one tap.

v1.why: A daily check-in sheet at bedtime is the last thing I want.

v2.why: Simplest of the three, but still makes me talk before it plays.

v3.why: Journal, wearables and reports are more stuff I'll never use at 11pm.

reason: A ten-minute session built for the meeting I'm dreading tomorrow is something I'd actually try, and $10 isn't the issue. But the free tier covers a few a week, which is all I need, and my watch data isn't really hooked in yet.
objection: I already have free apps and YouTube, so what am I paying for beyond more sessions I won't use?
would_change_my_mind: Real Apple Watch heart-rate or HRV shown before and after each session, so I can see it working on my numbers.

v1.why: Fake-looking percentages and an example chat that isn't mine.

v2.why: Quick to get a session for a specific stressful day.

v3.why: Same plus the wearable hook, which is the one thing that could make me pay later.

reason: I'll sign up day one because a session made from my own sentence is a cool idea and I'll show people. On my budget I'm living on the free tier, $10 a month is a bill I'd notice.
objection: Free apps and YouTube do this for nothing, so it's fun to try but not something I'd pay for.
would_change_my_mind: A much cheaper plan, around $3-4 a month, or a free month earned by inviting friends.

v1.why: Hamburger menu and coin clutter, feels older.

v2.why: Tabs and my own first session make it easy to come back.

v3.why: Most complete one; journal and stories without rankings are things I'd talk about.

reason: I'm awake scrolling most nights anyway, and tapping 'can't switch off' beats another hour of feeds. My therapist gives me homework between sessions and a five-chapter journey that adapts is close to that, so $10 is nothing next to what I spend on therapy.
objection: When I feel bad I don't want to type; if it needs paragraphs from me at 1am I'll stop.

v1.why: Percentages and 'Needs Improvement' would make me feel graded on bad nights.

v2.why: 'How do you feel now?' after each session is the right single question.

v3.why: Progress in my own words and a private journal are what I'd bring to therapy.

reason: Free with no card, I'd try it once before a deadline to see if it's real. I've never paid for one of these and I won't start at $10 on my salary.
objection: Will this actually calm me down or is it a gimmick with nice pictures?
would_change_my_mind: If it clearly worked the night before a big deadline a couple of times, and it cost under $5.

v1.why: Opens on someone else's chat, which makes it feel like a demo.

v2.why: Nicer, but I'd forget about it after the deadline passed.

v3.why: Best looking and least pushy, but I'd still go back to YouTube out of habit.

reason: I could afford it, but between work and the kids I barely get ten minutes, and when I do a free YouTube breathing video is already there. I'd try one session to see, then it'd probably sit unused.
objection: Is it actually going to help me, or is it another app that looks lovely and I never open after week one?
would_change_my_mind: A colleague telling me it got them through a hard month, and a two-minute option I can play in the car before work.

v1.why: Too many things to tap through before anything plays.

v2.why: Easier, but 'chapter 2 tomorrow' is one more thing I'd fall behind on.

v3.why: Kindest progress screen, but my problem is time, not the design.
